sections.html:
Chesterfield is a western suburb of St. Louis in St. Louis County, about 25 miles from downtown. Population was estimated at 49,309 on July 1, 2025. An owned home at the median is worth $472,500, and 77.6 percent of homes have owner occupants. Median gross rent is $1,644 and household income $133,037, so buyers here are well funded and picky about condition.

About a quarter of residents are 65 or older, so plenty of local sellers are downsizing or settling an estate, not moving for a job. Monthly owner costs run $2,464 with a mortgage and $946 without one, which tells you what a buyer will weigh against your asking price.

Parts of the city sit in the Missouri River floodplain, a valley once called Gumbo Flats. Ask your lender or title company whether your parcel needs flood insurance.

Two districts serve the city. Rockwood School District covers the western part and Parkway School District covers the east, and schools inside the city include Parkway Central, Parkway West and Marquette high schools. Buyers often ask the district first, so put it in your notes.

Repairs and additions go through the city's Planning Department. A building permit confirms that a project is structurally sound and meets building and zoning codes. Call the department before work on structure, additions or exterior changes.

The city's occupancy permit requirement is written for businesses: a permit or re-occupancy permit applies to every new business and every change of business use, tenancy or ownership. If you own a commercial space or a mixed property, that rule matters to your buyer. For an ordinary house sale, ask Chesterfield's Planning Department whether any permit applies to your address.

Occupancy approvals check compliance with city, county and fire district codes, so expect more than one office to be involved. Close any open permit before you list. Did an earlier owner skip a permit? Ask the department how to bring the work into compliance, and tell the buyer plainly. Surprises found during the buyer's inspection tend to cost more than the same issue raised early.

Parcel values are set by the county Assessor. Section 137.115 of state law calls for reassessment every odd-numbered year as of January 1. The assessor does not run the appeals board, which is independent. Appeals must be filed or postmarked by the second Monday in July. To challenge a value, keep recent sales, photos and repair estimates together, because the board wants evidence the Assessor's number is off. A seller who is about to list can also use a recent appraisal to support the asking price.

Bills come from the Collector of Revenue. Pay, or postmark your payment, by December 31 of the billed year. Payments made after that date are subject to up to 18 percent annual interest plus a 2 percent penalty under Missouri law.

The closing agent will confirm the current year, since the tax attaches to the house. Get the exact balance for your parcel from the collector.

Deeds for Chesterfield are recorded with the St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds, 41 S. Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. Bring or mail the notarized original with a check or money order payable to ROD, or file through an approved eRecording vendor. The original comes back within about a week of recording. Most owners leave this step to the title company.

The Missouri River valley flooded badly in 1993, and levees were raised afterward. The valley is now commercial, with Spirit of St. Louis Airport and a long strip of stores, but a house near the floodplain can still raise questions at closing. Your lender can say whether flood insurance is required, and any buyer's lender will raise it too. If you carry a policy, keep a copy of the declarations page for the buyer, since a transferable policy can be a selling point. Ask your agent or title company whether the buyer will need it before closing.

The soil in the valley turns to mud when wet, which is where the old Gumbo Flats name came from. Walk the lot after a heavy rain and note any pooling or foundation moisture, then fix drainage or disclose it before the buyer's inspector finds it.

sections.h2: Documents to gather before you list
sections.html:
A seller who has the paperwork ready can answer a buyer in a day instead of a week. Collect these first:

  • Your mortgage payoff letter from the lender.
  • The St. Louis County tax statement and proof that earlier years are paid.
  • Permit history, including any open or unclosed permit from past work.
  • The school district for the address, either Rockwood or Parkway.
  • Your recorded deed, available from the Clayton Recorder if you have lost it.

Ask the title company to run a search early. A stray lien, an unrecorded release or an open permit can hold up a closing for weeks. Each is simpler to clear before you sign a contract. Because the tax is a lien, the title company verifies the year's balance before closing and splits it between you and the buyer.

Because values are high and buyers are choosy, a Chesterfield house in good condition can attract the open market and sell on an agent's listing. If the house wants a new kitchen, roof or systems, or sits in an estate, a direct as-is purchase can work better, because the buyer takes on repairs.

Pull together the payoff letter, county tax statement, school district and permit history before anything else. With those in hand, you can compare an agent's net proceeds with a cash offer on equal terms.

If you are settling an estate, ask the title company early what court or probate papers they need before they will close, and whether anyone else holds an interest in the house. A cash buyer, with no lender to satisfy, can often close within a few weeks. The tax statement and deed recording do not change. Compare offers after counting closing costs, repairs a listing buyer would ask for, and carrying costs while the house sits. Ask every buyer, in writing, who pays for title, recording and any repair credits, and how many days they need to close. A clean contract with fewer conditions often nets more than a higher number that falls apart.

faqs.q: Which county records a Chesterfield deed?
faqs.a: St. Louis County, through the Recorder of Deeds at 41 S. Central Avenue in Clayton. Recording runs $26 for page one and $3 per extra page.

faqs.q: When are St. Louis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31 of the billed year, with the postmark counting for mailed payments. Later payments accrue up to 18 percent yearly interest plus a 2 percent penalty.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my St. Louis County value?
faqs.a: Appeals are filed with the independent Board of Equalization, due by the second Monday in July. Ask the board when the next window opens.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Chesterfield house in?
faqs.a: Rockwood School District serves the west side of the city and Parkway School District serves the east. Confirm the district for your address with the school district's boundary tools before listing.

faqs.q: Does Chesterfield's occupancy permit apply when I sell my home?
faqs.a: The occupancy permit requirement is aimed at businesses, covering new businesses and changes of use, tenancy or ownership. Call the Planning Department to confirm for your address.
